author: NPR Music
description:
Robin Hilton | November 20, 2026
When news broke earlier in the year that Mike D of the Beastie Boys had a new album on the way, it felt historic. It was the first-ever solo release from any member of the group, and the first new music at all from that universe since Adam Yauch (aka MCA) died in 2012. Thank You is bristling with reflections on the vast mysteries of life. The beats and bars hit hard before giving way to waves of reverb-soaked sweetness and even vulnerability, with an overwhelming sense of gratitude as the anchor.

Much of the vocals on Thank You are filtered through a swirling wash of effects, but here at the Desk, Mike D drops bars completely unadorned and in the clear. He and the band — which includes his sons, Skylar and Davis Diamond, on electronics — focus entirely on the new album, opening with "Make It Stop," a glitchy commentary on the age of self-destructive naval gazing.
